Measurement

/MEZH-er-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Measurement means the act of measuring, or the size, length, or amount established by measuring.

The carpenter double-checked every measurement before cutting the expensive walnut boards.

Worked Example

The tailor recorded each measurement — sleeve, shoulder, waist — before touching the fabric.

Each number the tailor writes down is a measurement: a size established by actually measuring with a tape, not by guessing. The word covers both the measuring itself and the figures it produces.

How Measurement Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dimension

dimension: a measurable extent such as length or width

reading

reading: the value an instrument shows

tally

tally: a running count that is recorded

Antonyms

guesswork

guesswork: judging without measuring or evidence

hunch

hunch: a feeling not based on facts or figures

How Strong Is It? — estimate → measurement → calibration

estimate vs. measurement

estimate vs. measurement: An estimate gives a rough idea of size; a measurement pins down the exact figure.

calibration vs. measurement

calibration vs. measurement: A measurement records one value; a calibration tests the measuring instrument itself against a perfect standard.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — measure

Root — measure: to find the size or amount (from Latin metiri, 'to measure')

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Measure (to find the size, from Latin metiri via Old French mesurer) + -ment (act or result): the act of measuring, or the figure you get when you do. Note that -ment attaches to the whole English verb, keeping its silent e: measure + -ment = measurement.

Use the root in a new word: immense

Use the root in a new word: immense: From the rim, the canyon looked immense — far too vast for the eye to measure.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral — everyday & technical

The suffix -ment turns the verb measure into a noun naming both the act ('careful measurement matters') and the result ('write down each measurement'). Keep the silent e when you spell it: measure + -ment. One more thing that sets it apart in this unit: its root is Latin metiri ('to measure'), not plere ('to fill') — it's the deliberate odd one out among these five -ment words.
